references.text: The same expression about God who brought Israel out of Egypt, with the same image of the wild ox's strength, repeated in Balaam's next oracle.
Moses reminds the people that the Lord brought them out of Egypt with a strong hand, a parallel to God's power in deliverance.
The horns of the wild ox are used as an image of Joseph's strength, the same animal imagery found in Balaam's prophecy.
God identifies Himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the foundation of the covenant relationship.
The horns of the wild ox are mentioned in a lament psalm; the same Hebrew word (re'em) is used to denote strength.
The horns of the wild ox are used as an image of exaltation and strength from God.
The wild ox (re'em) is described as an untamed and mighty animal, illustrating the power in the imagery Balaam uses.
God called His Son out of Egypt, a prophetic parallel to the deliverance mentioned in Balaam's oracle.
